Nyuserre Ini: Ancient Egyptian pharaoh of the Fifth Dynasty.
Worshipped by the peoples of the Andes as a mother goddess of space and time, this Inca deity is the wife of Pachacámac and mother of the sun and moon gods — who is she?
Despite his dyslexia, this Princeton-trained naval aviator became the first Ivy League astronaut — and commanding Apollo 12, the third human to set foot on the Moon. Who was he?
Pete Conrad: American astronaut and lunar explorer (1930–1999)
In Greek mythology, this last king of Troy during the Trojan War was the father of Hector, Paris, and Cassandra — who was he?
Priam: Mythological king of Troy. In Greek mythology, Priam (Ancient Greek: Πρίαμος, pronounced [prí.amos]) was the legendary and last king of Troy during the Trojan War.
Ascending the Siamese throne in 1782 following the deposition of King Taksin, this monarch became the first ruler of the Chakri dynasty and founded the city that is now Bangkok — who was he?
Rama I: King of Siam from 1782 to 1809.
A Labour politician who served two decades on the Kensington and Chelsea council, she also worked as a senior lecturer at Kingston University — who is she?
Rima Horton: English former councillor and economics lecturer (born 1947)
From 1904 to 1905, two empires clashed over rival ambitions in Manchuria and Korea, fighting major naval battles in the Yellow Sea and the Sea of Japan — which war was this?
Russo-Japanese War: 1904–1905 conflict in East Asia.
Founded in Japan in 2020 by Sohei Kamiya, this far-right populist party surged to more than 14 seats and third place in the 2025 House of Councillors election — which party?
Serving as Argentina's Minister of Economy from 2022 to 2023, this politician had earlier been Chief of Cabinet under Cristina Fernández de Kirchner and twice mayor of Tigre — who is he?
Sergio Massa: Argentine politician and lawyer (born 1972)
A media tycoon worth $6.8 billion at his death, which Italian served as prime minister across three separate governments between 1994 and 2011?
Silvio Berlusconi: Italian media tycoon and politician (1936–2023)
Writing under the pseudonym 'Frank Talk,' this South African activist led the grassroots Black Consciousness Movement against apartheid in the late 1960s and 1970s — who is he?
Thomas Seymour, 1st Baron Seymour of Sudeley
Steve Biko: South African anti-apartheid activist (1946–1977)

Punished in the underworld by standing in a pool beneath a fruit tree whose branches always pulled away from his grasp, this Greek mythological figure lent his name to the English word for teasing someone with something unreachable — who was he?
Tantalus: Greek mythological figure and son of Zeus.
Rising from Henry VIII's almoner to Lord Chancellor, this English cardinal controlled nearly every matter of state and held the Archbishopric of York — until his fall from royal favor. Who was he?
Thomas Wolsey: English statesman and cardinal (1473–1530)
The first Asian to lead the United Nations, this Burmese diplomat served a record ten years and one month as Secretary-General starting in 1961 — who was he?
U Thant: UN Secretary-General from 1961 to 1971.

Raiding, trading, and settling from Scandinavia across Europe, North Africa, and even Newfoundland between the late 8th and 11th centuries, this seafaring people helped establish Kievan Rus'. Who were they?
Vikings: Norse seafarers, merchants and raiders.

The first conflict of the Napoleonic Wars, this 1805–1806 struggle pitted Napoleon's France against an alliance of Britain, Austria, Russia, Naples, Sicily, and Sweden, and included the Battle of Trafalgar — which conflict?
War of the Third Coalition: 1805–1806 conflict during the Napoleonic Wars. The Royal Navy, however, assured its naval dominance at the Battle of Trafalgar in October 1805.

This Polish resistance leader deliberately got himself captured by the Germans in 1940 so he could infiltrate a notorious concentration camp and organize a resistance movement from within — who is he?
Serving as Japan's foreign minister from 2023 to 2024, she previously held the justice portfolio and worked on gender-equality policy under two different prime ministers — who is she?
Which of these people was born first?
Patrick Geddes (born 1854) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these was born first?
Ma Jun (mechanical engineer) (born 200) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these people was born first?
Jīvaka (born 401 BC) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four dates back furthest?
Fortran (founded 1957) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these is an astronomer?
Which of these four is a mathematician?
Hugh Everett III is a mathematician. Hugh Everett III (November 11, 1930 – July 19, 1982) was an American physicist who proposed the relative state interpretation of quantum mechanics.
What is the atomic number of Silver?
Silver: Silver is a chemical element; it has symbol Ag (from Latin argentum 'silver') and atomic number 47.
What is the atomic number of Calcium?
Calcium: Calcium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ca and atomic number 20.
In what year was Adrian Newey born?
Adrian Newey: Adrian Martin Newey (born 26 December 1958) is a British engineer, aerodynamicist, automotive designer, and motorsport executive.
In what year was Werner Heisenberg born?
Werner Heisenberg: Heisenberg published his Umdeutung paper in 1925, a major reinterpretation of old quantum theory.
In what year was Srinivasa Ramanujan born?
Srinivasa Ramanujan: Srinivasa Ramanujan Iyengar (22 December 1887 – 26 April 1920) was an Indian mathematician who worked during the early 20th century.
In what year did Ted Kaczynski die?
Ted Kaczynski: The FBI used the case identifier UNABOM (University and Airline Bombing) before his identity was known, resulting in the media naming him the "Unabomber".
In what year did Ada Lovelace die?
Ada Lovelace: Lovelace is often considered the first computer programmer.
In what year was Kepler's Supernova discovered?
Kepler's Supernova: SN 1604, also known as Kepler's Supernova, Kepler's Nova or Kepler's Star, was a Type Ia supernova that occurred in the Milky Way, in the constellation Ophiuchus.
PHP: Rasmus Lerdorf. PHP is a general-purpose scripting language geared towards web development.
Which company manufactures KAI KF-21 Boramae?
KAI KF-21 Boramae: Korea Aerospace Industries. The KAI KF-21 Boramae (Korean: KF-21 보라매; lit. 'KF-21 Hunting Hawk'; formerly KF-X; commonly KF-21) is a South Korean twin-engine fighter aircraft.
In which country did the Chengdu J-10 take place?

Chengdu J-10: People's Republic of China. It is produced by the Chengdu Aircraft Corporation (CAC) for the People's Liberation Army Air Force (PLAAF) of China, and exported to the Pakistan Air Force (PAF).
Who is credited with discovering Dubnium?
Dubnium: Joint Institute for Nuclear Research. Dubnium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Db and atomic number 105.
Who is credited with discovering Brainfuck?
Brainfuck: Urban Müller. Brainfuck is an esoteric programming language created in 1993 by Swiss student Urban Müller.
Who is credited with discovering Cobalt?
Cobalt: Georg Brandt. Cobalt is a chemical element; it has symbol Co and atomic number 27.
Often confused with the unrelated sweet chestnut, this large deciduous tree in the maple, soapberry, and lychee family bears hermaphroditic flowers — what tree is it?
Aesculus hippocastanum is a species of flowering plant in the maple, soapberry and lychee family Sapindaceae.
A member of the aminopenicillin family usually swallowed by mouth, this go-to remedy for ear infections, strep throat, and pneumonia is often paired with clavulanic acid — which antibiotic is it?
Amoxicillin is an antibiotic medication belonging to the aminopenicillin class of the penicillin family.
The 16th-largest family of flowering plants, this aromatic group includes cumin, fennel, and coriander alongside deadly relatives like water hemlock — which family?
Apiaceae is a family of mostly aromatic flowering plants named after the type genus Apium, and commonly known as the celery, carrot, or parsley family, or simply as umbellifers.
This gram-positive, spore-forming bacterium was the first ever proven experimentally to cause disease, laying the groundwork for germ theory in 1876 — which microbe?
Bacillus anthracis is a gram-positive and rod-shaped bacterium that causes anthrax, a deadly disease to livestock and, occasionally, to humans.

First flickering to life in octocorals some 540 million years ago and evolving independently at least 94 separate times, this glow is sometimes borrowed from symbiotic bacteria — what is the phenomenon?
Bioluminescence is the production of light by an organism as the result of a chemiluminescence reaction.
This rhythmic bodily process draws oxygen-rich air into the lungs and expels carbon dioxide, powering the cellular chemistry that turns food into energy — what process is it?
Breathing (respiring or ventilating) is the rhythmic process of inhaling air into the lungs providing oxygen, and exhaling the air removing carbon dioxide, in the gas exchange process.
Indigenous to Asia, this genus of flowering plants includes species like sativa, indica, and ruderalis, and is also commonly known as hemp when grown for non-drug purposes — name the genus?
Cannabis is a genus of flowering plants in the family Cannabaceae that is widely accepted as being indigenous to and originating from the continent of Asia.

The only living member of its genus, this big cat sprints at up to 104 km/h thanks to powerful hindlimbs, long legs, and a flexible spine, and wears black tear-like streaks down its face; which animal is it?
Cheetah (Acinonyx jubatus) is a species of large feline and the only living member of the genus Acinonyx.
Mostly belonging to the genus Naja, these venomous snakes are known for rearing upward and flaring a distinctive hood when threatened — name this common snake type?
Cobra is the common name of various venomous snakes, most of which belong to the genus Naja.
Tolerant of poor, sandy soil, this legume was domesticated in Africa millennia ago and is now grown far more in Nigeria and Niger than anywhere else on Earth — which crop?
Cowpea (Vigna unguiculata) is an annual herbaceous legume from the genus Vigna.

First patented in Germany in 1920, then independently synthesized by an American chemist in 1932 and marketed in German-speaking Europe as Permonid for its fast onset and short duration, what is this semi-synthetic opioid?
Desomorphine (or in some formulations known as Krokodil) is a semi-synthetic opioid commercialized by Roche, with powerful, fast-acting effects, such as sedation and analgesia.
Most of the 68 species sharing this name live in Eurasia and Africa, with only two found in North America — and "true" ones are merely a subfamily; what bird is it?
Eagle is the common name for certain large birds of prey within the family of the Accipitridae.

This genus's tapering spacing of stem nodes toward the tip is credited with inspiring John Napier's work on logarithms; today it's the sole living genus of an ancient, spore-producing plant lineage nicknamed horsetail — which genus?
Equisetum (horsetail) is the only living genus in Equisetaceae, a family of vascular plants that reproduce by spores rather than seeds.

Likely domesticated from the European polecat, with which it can still interbreed, this slender Mustelid pet weighs up to about two kilograms and comes in coats of black, brown or white — which animal?
Ferret (Mustela furo) is a small, domesticated species belonging to the family Mustelidae.
Caused by a loss of blood supply, this type of tissue death most commonly affects the feet and hands and can turn skin red or black. What condition is it?
Gangrene is a type of tissue death caused by a lack of blood supply. If the gangrene is caused by an infectious agent, it may present with a fever or sepsis.
Credited alongside Isaac Newton with inventing calculus, this German polymath also pioneered binary arithmetic and has been called the 'last universal genius' — who is he?
Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz was German polymath (1646–1716).
In their healthy state these vascular cushions in the anal canal actually help with stool control — it's only when they swell or inflame that they earn the nickname "piles." What are they?
Hemorrhoid (or haemorrhoids), also known as piles, are vascular structures in the anal canal.
This negatively charged ion, one oxygen bonded to one hydrogen, acts as a base and forms industrially vital salts like the sodium version used to make millions of tons of chemicals. What ion is it?
Hydroxide (occasionally hydroxyl ion) is a diatomic anion with chemical formula OH.

Acting as the eye's diaphragm in optical terms, this thin ring-shaped structure controls how much light reaches the retina by adjusting the pupil's size, and also determines a person's eye color — name this structure?

Iris (anatomy) (pl.: irides or irises) is a thin, ring-shaped structure in the eye in most mammals and birds that is responsible for controlling the diameter and size of the pupil, and thus the amount of light reaching the retina.
England's very first Astronomer Royal, he compiled a 3,000-star catalogue and even spotted Uranus — though he mistakenly logged it as a star. Who was he?
John Flamsteed (19 August 1646 - 31 December 1719) was an English astronomer and the first Astronomer Royal.
Alongside Robert Goddard and Hermann Oberth, this reclusive Russian scientist who lived in a log house near Kaluga is considered a founding father of modern rocketry — who is he?
At the time of her death, this French heiress and cosmetics-empire shareholder was the richest woman in the world, worth over $44 billion. Who is she?
Liliane Bettencourt (ne Schueller; 21 October 1922 - 21 September 2017) was a French heiress, socialite and businesswoman.
Which group of vividly colored, long-tailed New World parrots — prized in aviculture though some species face conservation concerns — belongs to the tribe Arini?
Macaw are a group of large New World parrots that are long-tailed and often colorful, in the tribe Arini.
It's the science and practice of diagnosing, treating, and preventing disease — from pharmaceuticals and surgery to splints, psychotherapy, and ionizing radiation. What is this field?
Medicine is the science and practice of caring for patients, managing the diagnosis, prognosis, prevention, treatment and palliation of their injury or disease, while promoting their health.

This synthetic prostaglandin drug can prevent stomach ulcers in people taking NSAIDs, induce labor, treat dangerous postpartum bleeding, and — alone or paired with another drug — end a pregnancy — what's the medication?

Misoprostol is a synthetic prostaglandin medication used to prevent and treat stomach and duodenal ulcers, induce labor, cause an abortion, and treat postpartum bleeding due to poor contraction of the uterus.

Native to the Horn of Africa and nicknamed the 'sand puppy,' this burrowing rodent is the only mammal that's a cold-blooded thermoconformer — and lives in an insect-like colony with a single breeding queen. What is it?
Naked mole-rat (Heterocephalus glaber), also known as the sand puppy, is a burrowing rodent native to the Horn of Africa and parts of Kenya, notably in Somali regions.
Built from proteins, DNA, and RNA around specific chromosomal regions, this nuclear structure is being studied as a target for cancer chemotherapy — what is it?
Nucleolus (pl.: nucleoli) is the largest structure in the nucleus of eukaryotic cells.
Founded as a science by Georges Cuvier in 1796, when he demonstrated evidence for extinction, this field studies prehistoric life mainly through fossils — what's the discipline?
Paleontology is the scientific study of the life of the past, mainly but not exclusively through the study of fossils.
This inflammation of the lining of the abdominal cavity can be caused by a ruptured appendix, a perforated ulcer, or pancreatitis, and may lead to shock if untreated. What condition is it?
Peritonitis is inflammation of the localized or generalized peritoneum, the lining of the inner wall of the abdomen and covering of the abdominal organs.
Used in randomized clinical trials to gauge a treatment's true efficacy, this inert pill, injection, or sham surgery has no pharmaceutical effect of its own — what is it?
Placebo (pluh-) is a medicine or treatment intended to appear genuine to its recipient, but which has no pharmaceutical effect.

This mammal genus includes a familiar, masked, ring-tailed nocturnal visitor common across North America, plus two lesser-known tropical relatives; its closest kin are the ring-tailed cats and cacomistles. What animal is this?
Procyon (genus) is a genus of nocturnal mammals comprising three species commonly known as raccoons in the family Procyonidae.
A medium-sized tropical tree native to Southeast Asia, it's a close relative of the lychee and longan and shares its name with the edible fruit it bears — what is it?
Rambutan (Nephelium lappaceum) is a medium-sized tropical tree in the family Sapindaceae.

This English X-ray crystallographer's photographs were crucial to unraveling the structure of DNA, yet her contribution went largely unrecognized in her lifetime, earning her posthumous nicknames like "the wronged heroine" — who was she?
Rosalind Franklin (25 July 1920 - 16 April 1958) was an English chemist and X-ray crystallographer.

Seven living species make up this group of ocean-dwelling reptiles, five of which are threatened with extinction — one species, found only near Australia, Papua New Guinea, and Indonesia, is not — name this group?
Sea turtle (superfamily Chelonioidea), sometimes called marine turtles, are reptiles of the order Testudines and of the suborder Cryptodira.
Which urban model uses digital technology and data from citizens, buildings, and cameras to improve sustainability, efficiency, and social inclusion?
Smart city is an urban model that leverages technology, human capital, and governance to improve sustainability, efficiency, and social inclusion, which are considered goals for cities of the future.
This Taiwanese-American software engineer co-founded and served as CTO of a massively popular video-sharing platform before later building MixBit through his company AVOS Systems — who is he?
Steve Chen (Wade-; born August 25, 1978) is a Taiwanese-American software engineer and Internet entrepreneur who is a co-founder and ex-CTO of YouTube.

A carnivorous marsupial formerly found across mainland Australia but now confined to Tasmania, this animal became the world's largest carnivorous marsupial after the thylacine's extinction in 1936. What is this fierce creature?
Tasmanian devil (Sarcophilus harrisii; palawa kani: purinina) is a carnivorous marsupial of the family Dasyuridae.

Sitting at the organizational level between individual cells and a full organ, this biological term for a functional grouping of similar cells derives from a French word meaning 'to weave' — what is it?
Tissue (biology) is an assembly of similar cells and their extracellular matrix from the same embryonic origin that together carry out a specific function.
This medical specialty, whose name derives from the Greek word for urine, covers surgical and medical treatment of the urinary tract and the male reproductive organs — name this field?

Urology (from Greek ouron "urine" and - -logia "study of"), also known as genitourinary surgery, is the branch of medicine that focuses on surgical and medical diseases of the urinary system and the male reproductive organs.
Packing a mass comparable to the Sun into a volume the size of Earth, this dense stellar remnant radiates residual heat rather than nuclear fusion — what is it?
White dwarf is a very dense type of star: in an Earth-sized volume, it packs a mass that is comparable to the Sun.
This Danish physicist shared the 1975 Nobel for work on the structure of the atomic nucleus — making him and his famous father one of the rare parent-child pairs to each win the prize. Who was he?
Native to the arid Americas, most rosettes of this succulent genus flower gloriously just once before dying, earning one species the nickname 'century plant' — what genus is it?
Meaning 'different lizard' and first described in 1877 by Othniel Marsh, most fossils of this Late Jurassic predator come from North America's Morrison Formation — which dinosaur?

Found along the Andes and Pacific coasts of South America, this enormous New World vulture is one of the largest flying birds by wingspan, with males sporting a fleshy comb atop a bald red head — which species is it?
Andean condor: Species of bird. The Andean condor (Vultur gryphus) is a South American New World vulture and is the only extant member of the genus Vultur.
Commonly called a canker sore, this recurring condition produces benign mouth ulcers that heal within 7 to 10 days but often return three to six times a year — what is it?
Aphthous stomatitis: Common oral condition lasting 7–10 days.
Larger than a meteoroid but smaller than a planet, most of these rocky, metallic, or icy bodies orbit between Mars and Jupiter — what are they called?
Asteroid: Minor planet found within the inner Solar System.
Named by naturalist Constantine Rafinesque in 1815, this predatory saltwater fish prowls near coral reefs and is a favorite target of sport anglers worldwide — what is it?
Also called the bearcat, this dark, shaggy, tree-dwelling Asian viverrid sports a prehensile tail and musk glands that famously smell of buttered popcorn — what is it?
Binturong: Asian mammal also known as a bearcat.
Developed alongside the 707 airliner from the same prototype, this narrower, shorter jet became the U.S. Air Force's first jet-powered refueling tanker in 1957 — name the aircraft?
Boeing KC-135 Stratotanker: US military aerial refueling and transport aircraft.
Sold under the brand name Pulmicort, this steroid drug treats asthma when inhaled but also comes as a nasal spray for allergies and a rectal foam for bowel disease — which medication?
This highly contagious virus, spread through feces, can kill up to 91% of untreated dogs and wolves and also strikes foxes, cats, and skunks — what is it?
Canine parvovirus: Contagious virus mainly affecting dogs.
Native to Madagascar, this flowering plant known as the Madagascar periwinkle is the source of two major cancer-fighting drugs — what is it?
Catharanthus roseus: Species of flowering plant in the family Apocynaceae.
Its roasted root has long served as a coffee substitute, while today its extracted inulin shows up as a sweetener and fiber additive in packaged foods — which blue-flowered plant?
Chicory: Flowering plant in the daisy family.
Found in birds, reptiles, amphibians, and egg-laying mammals like the platypus, which single all-purpose body opening handles digestion, reproduction, and waste?
The heaviest songbird on Earth and the most widely distributed of all the corvids, this all-black passerine averages 25 inches long across the Northern Hemisphere — what is it?
Common raven: Large, black species of passerine bird.
First described in 1963, this rare disorder from a partial deletion on chromosome 5 gets its French name from the distinctive feline-sounding cry of affected infants — what is it called?
Cri du chat syndrome: Human medical condition.

This English broadcaster is the only person to have won BAFTA Awards in black-and-white, colour, high-definition, 3D, and 4K — a span made possible by a presenting career that began with Zoo Quest in 1954. Who is this natural historian?
David Attenborough: English broadcaster and natural historian (born 1926)

A lean, wedge-skulled medium canine found in Australia and split off from the New Guinea singing dog, this animal's very classification — dog, wolf, or its own species — is still hotly debated — what is it?
Dingo: Canid species native to Australia.

Anatomically like us, some of the oldest remains of this species come from Ethiopia's Omo-Kibish site, dated to roughly 233,000 to 196,000 years ago — what term distinguishes them from archaic humans?
Early modern human: Old Stone Age ''Homo sapiens''
Affecting roughly 10% of women of reproductive age — nearly 200 million worldwide — this disease occurs when tissue like the uterine lining grows on the ovaries, bowel, or elsewhere. What is it?

Exercise, laughter, dancing, and romantic love can all trigger this intense state of well-being via the brain's pleasure centers — though it's also a symptom of mania and the lure of addictive drugs. What is it?
Euphoria: Intense feelings of well-being. Euphoria (yoo-FOR-ee-ə) is the experience (or affect) of pleasure or excitement and intense feelings of well-being and happiness.
This genus of small-to-medium wildcats — ranging from the diminutive black-footed cat to the larger jungle cat — also includes humanity's domestic pet, the housecat — which genus?
Found at the end of the leg and typically featuring claws or nails, which weight-bearing body part enables locomotion in many vertebrates?
Foot: Anatomical structure found in vertebrates.
Once classified under two different bacterial genera, this nonmotile coccobacillus forms small gray colonies on chocolate agar and has its own colistin-oxolinic acid selective medium — which species?
Gardnerella vaginalis: Species of bacterium. Gardnerella vaginalis is a species of Gram-variable-staining facultative anaerobic bacteria.
Nicknamed the "silent thief of sight" because it steals vision slowly, this group of eye diseases damages the optic nerve and is closely tied to raised pressure inside the eye — what is it?
Glaucoma: Group of eye diseases related to poor retinal and nerve perfusion.
With long, whip-like antennae and a global range except Antarctica, this insect family — known as true crickets — includes burrowing giants that dig meter-deep tunnels. What is the family called?
Gryllidae: Family of crickets. The family Gryllidae contains the subfamilies and genera which entomologists now term true crickets.
This German physicist was the first to conclusively demonstrate the electromagnetic waves predicted by James Clerk Maxwell's equations — who is he?
Introduced in 1948 by a French naturalist, this taxonomic tribe groups humans together with chimpanzees and bonobos, but excludes gorillas — which tribe?
Hominini: Tribe of mammals. The Hominini (hominins) form a taxonomic tribe of the subfamily Homininae (hominines).

Responsible for nearly half a million deaths each year, this condition occurs when the body produces or absorbs more heat than it can dissipate, most often from heat stroke or a drug reaction — what condition?
Hyperthermia: Elevated body temperature due to failed thermoregulation.
This concept in calculus, a continuous analog of a sum, computes the signed area under a curve and pairs with differentiation as one of the field's two fundamental operations?
This fragrant genus of shrubs and vines in the olive family is grown in vast quantities in one Egyptian village that supplies much of the world's perfume industry — which plant?
Jasmine: Genus of flowering plant in the olive family Oleaceae.
Born Giulia Maddalena Angela in Italy, this physician became a leading freethinker and activist for women's rights and social reform in early-20th-century Argentina — who is she?
Julieta Lanteri: Argentine doctor and activist (1873–1932)
Native to southern China and roughly the size of a large olive, which citrus fruit closely resembles a tiny orange and is famously cold-hardy?
Kumquat: Species of small fruit-bearing tree.
Spread by rats, dogs and other animals, this bacterial blood infection has an acute, jaundice-causing severe form known as Weil's disease — what's the condition?
Leptospirosis: Blood infection caused by bacteria.
Nicknamed the 'Dragon Lady,' this single-engine American spy plane flew covert missions above 70,000 feet over the Soviet Union, China, and Cuba from the 1950s — what is it?

This German physician and sexologist founded the Scientific-Humanitarian Committee, mounting what's been called the first advocacy for homosexual and transgender rights — and the Nazis revoked his citizenship in 1933. Who was he?
Born in Erfurt in 1864, this German jurist-turned-scholar became one of the founding figures of sociology before a breakdown following his father's death halted his teaching — who was he?
Max Weber: German sociologist, jurist, and political economist (1864–1920)
This field studies how we study — analyzing, comparing, and evaluating the procedures researchers use to gather and interpret data, shaped by underlying philosophical assumptions. What is it called?
Nicknamed the 'powerhouse of the cell' after a phrase popularized in a 1957 magazine article, this double-membraned organelle generates ATP through respiration — which organelle?
Mitochondrion: Organelle in eukaryotic cells responsible for respiration.
This semiaquatic rodent swims using webbed hind feet while its scaly, flattened tail works mainly as a rudder for steering — what is it?
Muskrat: Species of rodent. The muskrat or common muskrat (Ondatra zibethicus) is a medium-sized semiaquatic rodent.
Popularized by neurologist George Beard in the 1860s, this diagnosis described fatigue, anxiety, and heart palpitations often blamed on the stresses of modern life — what was the condition called?
This burrowing, semiaquatic South American rodent munches river-plant stems and was shipped worldwide by fur farmers, only to become a destructive invasive pest — which animal is it?
Nutria: Semi-aquatic rodent from South America.
Farmed largely around a South African town, this flightless bird is the heaviest bird alive and can sprint 70 km/h — the fastest of any bird on land. What is it?
Ostrich: Genus of largest living birds.
This American physician-turned-clown founded the Gesundheit Institute in 1989 and travels the world dressing up to bring humor to hospital patients — who is he?
Named from a Tupi-Guarani word for tobacco filtered through French, this South American flowering plant genus is a garden hybrid favorite — which plant?
Petunia: Genus of flowering plants. The popular flower of the same name derived its epithet from the French, which took the word pétun, 'tobacco', from a Tupi–Guarani language.

Not approved for general use in the US but sold across Europe for conditions such as vertigo and cortical myoclonus, this drug is a cyclic derivative of the neurotransmitter GABA and belongs to the 'racetam' group — what is it?
Domesticated some 7,000 to 10,000 years ago in what is now southern Peru, this starchy underground tuber belongs to the nightshade family — what is it?
Potato: Starchy tuber used as a staple food.
This Greco-Roman scholar authored the Almagest on astronomy and the Geography, a treatise on maps and geographic knowledge — who is he?

A pioneer in optical character recognition and speech synthesis, this futurist inventor received the National Medal of Technology from President Clinton in 1999 for his outlook on AI and life extension — who is he?
Ray Kurzweil: American computer scientist, author and futurist (born 1948)
Often called the first modern chemist, which 17th-century Anglo-Irish natural philosopher described the inverse relationship between a gas's pressure and volume in a law that bears his name?
Named for the genus of the Atlantic salmon, this family of cold-water fish also includes trout, char, and grayling — what family is it?
People with this anxiety disorder are fully capable of speech but fall silent in specific situations or around specific people, even when staying quiet brings shame or punishment — what is it called?
Selective mutism: Anxiety disorder blocking speech. Selective mutism usually co-exists with social anxiety disorder.
This layer of tissue covering a vertebrate's body serves three main functions: protection, regulation, and sensation?
Skin: Soft outer covering organ of vertebrates.

First described in 1915 by a German paleontologist from Egyptian fossils that were destroyed during World War II, this dinosaur genus wasn't represented by new material until the early 2000s — which genus?
Spinosaurus: Genus of spinosaurid dinosaur. The genus was known first from Egyptian remains discovered in 1912 and described by German palaeontologist Ernst Stromer in 1915.

This small nocturnal marsupial has membranes stretching from its forelegs to hindlegs that let it soar between trees, and its scientific name translates to 'short-headed rope-dancer' — what animal is it?
Sugar glider: Species of Australian marsupial.
A staple from the Caribbean to Oceania to East Asia, this Araceae-family plant is prized for the starchy underground corm it grows much like a yam — what is it?
Taro: Species of plant. Taro (Colocasia esculenta) is a root vegetable.
This French economist's best-selling 2013 book argued that capital returns persistently outpace economic growth, driving ever-rising wealth inequality — who is he?
Inside a ribosome, this cellular process reads messenger RNA three nucleotides at a time to build a chain of amino acids into protein — what is it called?
Translation (biology): Cellular process of protein synthesis. Translation is the process in biological cells in which proteins are produced using RNA molecules as templates.
